candidates.statement: We must stress, that one can see the elements of the dualization idea in papers [@babelon; @gervais2; @curtho; @teschner] devoted to the Liouville model itself, and in [@BLZ1; @BLZ2; @BLZ3; @BPZ] within the framework of conformal field theory.

They will attract our attention in the next couple of (sub)sections where we shall try to treat the Magri bracket and the "chiral Hamiltonian" $L_0$ as a stand-alone dynamical system, not for the first time of course.
We shall review some earlier attempts to get it properly discretized and quantized.
It should be noted however that the latter only emerges in a rather tricky continuous limit, while the simplest limit leads to the free equation ([\[cr\]](#cr){reference-type="ref" reference="cr"}).

Which is a little unfortunate, for however essential a part has the Volterra system been playing in the soliton theory, there must be something wrong about a nonlinear equation emulating a linear one.
So, in the rest of this section we shall be looking at that motion, then we shall try to guess how it could be lifted back to the Magri--Virasoro case.

candidates.section_title: It has to do with braids

candidates.statement: If that is to be, the "global" relations ought to remain the same as in the braid group $$d_1d_2\ldots d_{N-1}=d_2d_3\ldots d_N =\cdots=d_Nd_{N+1}\ldots d_{2N-2}\;,$$ or equivalently $$\tag{\ref{cr}\(''\)} \hat d_n=d_{n-1}=Q^{-1}d_nQ\qquad\qquad Q=d_1d_2\ldots d_{N-1}\; ,$$ but this time each generator should interfere not only with the nearest neighbours but also with the second-nearest ones $$d_md_n=d_nd_m\qquad\text{if }|m-n| \not\equiv1\text{ and }2\pmod{N} ,$$ just like it was in bracket ([\[mb\]](#mb){reference-type="ref" reference="mb"}$'$) of course.
In continuum, the Liouville equation may be considered as a compatibility condition for the Liouville formula overloaded with Möbius-invariance.
